evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites this mouse study.

claim: Another Trpv6-/- mutant mouse line reported by Chen et al. had normal blood Ca2+ concentration and normal bone formation, but with an increased number of osteoclasts.
source: Another Trpv6-/- mutant mouse line reported by Chen et al., however, had normal blood Ca2+ concentration and normal bone formation, but with an increased number of osteoclasts (Chen et al., 2014).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites this mouse study showing different phenotypes.

claim: A third Trpv6-/- mutant mouse model showed reduced fertility in male only.
source: A third Trpv6-/- mutant mouse model showed reduced fertility in male only (Weissgerber et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites this mouse study.

claim: Zebrafish embryos continuously lose Ca2+ and other ions into the surrounding hypo-osmotic environments and must constantly take up Ca2+ from the habitat to survive.
source: Zebrafish embryos continuously lose Ca2+ and other ions into the surrounding hypo-osmotic environments and must constantly take up Ca2+ from the habitat to survive (Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this physiological difference and cites a reference.

claim: In mammals, there is another closely related TRPV sub-family member, TRPV5.
source: In mammals, there is another closely related TRPV sub-family member, TRPV5.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this genetic difference between mammals and zebrafish.

claim: TRPV5 plays similar roles in the transcellular Ca2+ transport pathway, although it is mainly expressed in the kidney.
source: TRPV5 plays similar roles in the transcellular Ca2+ transport pathway, although it is mainly expressed in the kidney (Hoenderop et al., 2005).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes TRPV5 function and cites a reference.

claim: TRPV5 expression in the intestine is elevated in Trpv6 mutant mice.
source: It has been shown that TRPV5 expression in the intestine is elevated in Trpv6 mutant mice (Woudenberg-Vrenken et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites this compensatory mechanism in mice.

claim: Zebrafish genome has a single trpv6 gene and lacks genetic redundancy with TRPV5.
source: In comparison, zebrafish genome has a single trpv6 gene and lacks this genetic redundancy (Vanoevelen et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this genetic difference and cites a reference.

claim: Fura-2 Ca2+ imaging studies in cultured mammalian cells transfected with TRPV6 indicated that this channel is constitutively open.
source: Fura-2 Ca2+ imaging studies in cultured mammalian cells transfected with TRPV6 indicated that this channel is constitutively open (Vennekens et al., 2000).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites this previous finding.

claim: A recent study has provided structural and functional evidence that TRPV6 is constitutively active.
source: Although another study failed to detect spontaneous channel activity by patch-clamp recording in cells transfected with TRPV6, a recent study has provided structural and functional evidence that TRPV6 is constitutively active (McGoldrick et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites this recent structural study.

claim: Other studies have reported that TRPV6 activity is activated by a reduction in [Ca2+]i concentration, and inactivated by higher [Ca2+]i in mammalian cells.
source: Other studies have reported that TRPV6 activity is activated by a reduction in [Ca2+]i concentration, and inactivated by higher [Ca2+]i in mammalian cells (Nilius et al., 2000; Yue et al., 2001).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites these studies showing calcium-dependent regulation.

claim: The Trpv6 channel is constitutively open in NaR cells in vivo.
source: Our in vivo Ca2+ imaging results showed that the Trpv6 channel is constitutively open in NaR cells in vivo.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly concludes this based on the GCaMP7a imaging experiments.

claim: It was thought that Ca2+ transporting epithelial cells maintain low levels of [Ca2+]i using the cytosolic Ca2+ binding protein.
source: It was thought that Ca2+ transporting epithelial cells, being continuously challenged by Ca2+ traffic from the apical side, maintain low levels of [Ca2+]i using the cytosolic Ca2+ binding protein (Hoenderop et al., 2005).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites this conventional view.

claim: The in vivo imaging findings challenge the conventional view that Ca2+ transporting cells maintain low [Ca2+]i levels.
source: The in vivo imaging findings made in this study challenge this conventional view.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states that their findings contradict the conventional model.

claim: Maintaining high [Ca2+]i levels in Ca2+ transporting cells is likely beneficial to the organism because it keeps these cells in differentiated state and functioning as Ca2+ transporting units.
source: We postulate that maintaining high [Ca2+]i levels in these Ca2+ transporting cells is likely beneficial to the organism because it keeps these cells in differentiated state and functioning as Ca2+ transporting units.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly proposes this hypothesis based on their findings.

claim: A [Ca2+]i-regulated PP2A isoform(s) likely acts downstream of TRPV6/Trpv6 and regulates the quiescent state in epithelial cells.
source: Our in vivo findings, together with the in vitro findings indicate that a [Ca2+]i-regulated PP2A isoform(s) likely acts downstream of TRPV6/Trpv6 and regulates the quiescent state in epithelial cells.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly proposes this mechanistic model based on the data.

claim: Compromising PP2A activity delays cell cycle exit in Drosophila.
source: This is in good agreement with a recent study showing that compromising PP2A activity delays cell cycle exit in Drosophila (Sun and Buttitta, 2015).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites this supporting study from Drosophila.

claim: The TRPV6-[Ca2+]i-PP2A signaling axis appears to be conserved in human colon carcinoma cells.
source: The TRPV6-[Ca2+]i-PP2A signaling axis appears to be conserved in human colon carcinoma cells because siRNA-mediated knockdown or inhibition of TRPV6 increased LoVo cell proliferation.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly concludes conservation based on the human cell experiments.

claim: PR72/130 and PR70 possess two conserved EF hand motifs.
source: Recent studies suggest that PR72/130 and PR70, 2 members of the B' family, possess two conserved EF hand motifs (termed EF1 and EF2) and increasing [Ca2+]i increased the holoenzyme assembly and phosphatase activity (Kurimchak et al., 2013; Magenta et al., 2008).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites these studies on calcium-dependent PP2A regulation.

claim: Increasing [Ca2+]i increased PP2A holoenzyme assembly and phosphatase activity.
source: Recent studies suggest that PR72/130 and PR70, 2 members of the B' family, possess two conserved EF hand motifs (termed EF1 and EF2) and increasing [Ca2+]i increased the holoenzyme assembly and phosphatase activity (Kurimchak et al., 2013; Magenta et al., 2008).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites these mechanistic studies.

claim: [Ca2+]i-dependent m-calpain degrades PR72 and PR130 into a 45 kDa fragment.
source: Another mechanism involves the action of [Ca2+]i-dependent m-calpain: m-calpain degrades PR72 and PR130 into a 45 kDa fragment (Janssens et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites this alternative mechanism.

claim: The 45 kDa fragment PR45 is resistant to further degradation and exhibits enhanced PP2A activity.
source: This fragment, termed as PR45, is resistant to further degradation and exhibits enhanced PP2A activity.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the properties of this fragment.

claim: The calpain-mediated proteolytic activation of PP2A depends on the EF hand integrity.
source: These two mechanisms may be related because the calpain-mediated proteolytic activation of PP2A depends on the EF hand integrity (Janssens et al., 2009).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites this mechanistic connection.

claim: Approximately 90% of human cancers arise in epithelial tissues.
source: Approximately 90% of human cancers arise in epithelial tissues and over-proliferation is one of the cancer hallmarks (Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this cancer statistic and cites a reference.

claim: Over-proliferation is one of the cancer hallmarks.
source: Approximately 90% of human cancers arise in epithelial tissues and over-proliferation is one of the cancer hallmarks (Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and cites the hallmarks of cancer paper.

claim: The IGF signaling pathway is one of the most frequently mutated signaling pathways in epithelial tissue-derived cancers, including colon and prostate cancers.
source: The IGF signaling pathway is one of the most frequently mutated signaling pathways in epithelial tissue-derived cancers, including colon and prostate cancers (Massoner et al., 2010).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this and cites a reference.

claim: The IGF2 gene and IRS2 gene are frequently gained in colon cancer.
source: The IGF2 gene and IRS2 gene are frequently gained in colon cancer (Cancer Genome Atlas Network, 2012) and have been proposed as a colorectal cancer 'driver' oncogenes (Day et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites these cancer genomics findings.

claim: IGF2 and IRS2 have been proposed as colorectal cancer 'driver' oncogenes.
source: The IGF2 gene and IRS2 gene are frequently gained in colon cancer (Cancer Genome Atlas Network, 2012) and have been proposed as a colorectal cancer 'driver' oncogenes (Day et al., 2013).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites this cancer biology interpretation.

claim: TRPV6 gene is frequently up-regulated in prostate, colon, and other cancer tissues.
source: TRPV6 gene is frequently up-regulated in prostate, colon, and other cancer tissues (Lehen'kyi et al., 2012; Prevarskaya et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites these cancer expression studies.

claim: It is unclear whether the elevated TRPV6 expression promotes tumor growth or it is an adaptive response.
source: At present, it is unclear whether the elevated TRPV6 expression promotes tumor growth or it is an adaptive response (Lehen'kyi et al., 2012; Prevarskaya et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states this uncertainty in the field.

claim: Knockdown or overexpression of TRPV6 in cultured cancer cells showed mixed effects in increasing/decreasing proliferation and/or apoptosis.
source: Knockdown or overexpression of TRPV6 in cultured cancer cells showed mixed effects in increasing/decreasing proliferation and/or apoptosis (Chow et al., 2007; Lehen'kyi et al., 2007; Lehen'kyi et al., 2012; Raphaël et al., 2014; Skrzypski et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly cites multiple studies showing inconsistent results.
